note: Positive and defeating cases for the asset objects in SPEC.md, judged by conformance/asset_objects.py. Each case states a world; a key omitted is unknown rather than satisfied. Every defeating case is the base world with exactly one thing wrong, so a failing case names its invariant and nothing else. The oracle imports no participant code, so these grade the logical model and hold before any implementation carries the objects. decisions/0077 owns the rulings.

cases.proves: an asset is a governed identity and never holds bytes
an asset carrying payload_address is bytes wearing an identity
an asset names a declared type
an asset naming an undeclared type is refused TYPE_UNDECLARED
a description names the asset it describes
a description targeting a payload address describes bytes
one type is declared once
redeclaring an asset_type_id is refused STALE_STATE
a declared type governs, an observed media type does not
an observed media type standing in for a declared type
a version carries every required constituent role
a version omitting a required role is judged at record time
a version holds an entry set and reaches bytes through it
a version carrying a payload assumes a single payload
every entry names a part of this asset and a state of that part
an entry naming an unknown part resolves to nothing
every entry declares where its constituent sits
an entry with no placement cannot say where a part is
lineage and derivation are separate fields
a stored exclusive role collapses two independent facts
one entry set carries one content digest
two digests over one entry set make the address meaningless
a part is a constituent identity carrying no path
a part carrying a logical path is a file wearing an identity
a part occupies a role its asset's type declares
a part in an undeclared role is arbitrary description
a content state says what it is and not where it came from
a singular source on a content state makes provenance state
a representation carries only intrinsic facts
a filename in a representation is placement leaking down
a content state names an address, not a storage form
a chunk list on a content state puts storage in the contract
two content states may hold identical bytes and stay distinct records
one part_version_id declared twice is one record, not two
many observations may point at one content state
an observation of no content state observes nothing
a move is the same content state in a new placement
MOVED claimed across two content states on equal payload alone
a rename is a new asset version over the same part version - same part, same content state, different composition state
